title: Sell Mineral Rights in Tumbling Shoals, AR
primaryKeyword: sell mineral rights tumbling shoals ar
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Tumbling Shoals, AR
metaDescription: Tumbling Shoals, AR mineral rights in Cleburne County's Fayetteville Shale gas trend near Heber Springs. Legacy leases from the mid-2000s boom.
heroLead: Tumbling Shoals sits in Cleburne County near Greers Ferry Lake, an area better known for lake tourism than for oil and gas, though the Fayetteville Shale reached under it just the same.
intro: Cleburne County was part of the broader Fayetteville Shale leasing wave during the mid-2000s, and the area around Tumbling Shoals saw gas leases signed alongside the rest of the county even as its surface economy leaned heavily on the lake and tourism. Mineral rights here have often gone unnoticed by families more focused on lake property than what lies beneath it.

sections.heading: Lake Country With Underground History
paragraphs: It's easy for a family with lakefront or near-lake property to overlook that the mineral rights underneath their land are a completely separate asset, one that may still be leased, producing, or simply sitting unaddressed since a lease was signed decades ago. Confirming what you actually hold starts with a title check, not with what the surface property is currently used for.

sections.heading: Checking Cleburne County Records
paragraphs: The Cleburne County Circuit Clerk's office in Heber Springs holds the deed, probate, and lease records relevant to Tumbling Shoals-area tracts. Because this part of the Fayetteville Shale saw somewhat less intensive drilling than counties closer to the play's core, valuation on a given tract depends heavily on its specific position and lease status rather than a general assumption about the area.

faqs.question: My property near Tumbling Shoals is mostly used as a lake getaway. Do I still have mineral rights to worry about?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it's worth checking. Surface use for recreation doesn't affect whether mineral rights exist separately underneath the property or whether they were leased at some point.

faqs.question: Was Cleburne County heavily drilled during the Fayetteville Shale boom?
faqs.answer: It saw leasing and some drilling activity, generally less dense than the core counties closer to the play's center, so tract-specific status matters more here than in more heavily developed areas.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my family's old lease near Tumbling Shoals is still active?
faqs.answer: We can check the lease against Cleburne County recordings and state production data to confirm whether it's still being held by production or has expired.

faqs.question: Does Greers Ferry Lake tourism affect mineral rights value in this area?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Tourism and lake property values reflect the surface market, while mineral rights value is tied to the gas play beneath the land and its lease or production status.
